sources.title: Unified 4D World Action Modeling from Video Priors with Asynchronous Denoising

omissions: Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.

The extraction-only visual gap was resolved by inspecting the retained PDF figures, tables, equations and algorithms. All seven supplied text chunks were read individually, including references and Appendices A–E. Reference pages 10–15 were read as text, not rendered.

Identity/edition note: the inspected title page identifies arXiv:2604.26694v2 [cs.RO], 7 May 2026, with the catalog title and all ten authors. The catalog submission date is 29 April 2026; this report concerns the supplied v2 artifact. No earlier version or revision comparison was supplied, so changes from v1 remain unverified.
No external project media, code or separate supplement was inspected, and no experiment was reproduced. The project link does not establish code availability.
figuresReviewed: Figure 2, PDF p. 4: architecture and ANS

synopsis: X-WAM adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to predict robot actions, future states and multi-view RGB-D observations together. A one-way depth branch adds geometric supervision, while asynchronous denoising releases actions before completing video generation. The paper reports strong simulated manipulation and reconstruction results plus a small physical earphone-packing evaluation. Its central tradeoff is useful spatial supervision without depth decoding during every action step; limited temporal context and delayed control remain unresolved.

problem.text: A unified robot model must predict executable movement and coherent visual and geometric futures despite their different computational demands. The authors argue that pixel-only world-action models lack spatial grounding, while synchronized video/action diffusion makes control wait for expensive video synthesis. X-WAM addresses both problems within a shared predictor.

contributions.text: A replicated, interleaved depth branch learns inverse depth from shared features without adding depth tokens to the main denoising sequence.
Asynchronous Noise Sampling couples training noise levels and explicitly includes clean-action conditioning, supporting early action release and subsequent video-only denoising.

outputs: Eight future multi-view RGB and depth frames
Fused 3D reconstructions using RGB-D and camera poses

steps.name: Encode a shared sequence
steps.detail: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B supplies the video DiT and causal VAE. MLPs encode/decode states and actions. Initial observation/state tokens remain clean; future tokens use bidirectional full attention. View embeddings distinguish cameras, and temporal RoPE aligns eight future video/state samples with thirty-two actions.

steps.name: Read geometry through an auxiliary branch
steps.detail: After the shared trunk, ten replicated final blocks form a depth branch. Each reads the main branch’s input at the corresponding layer; the main branch cannot attend back to depth. Depth maps use the RGB VAE representation after three-channel replication, with inverse-depth MSE supervision.

steps.name: Recover a common spatial frame
steps.detail: Predicted end-effector poses and fixed hand-eye calibration yield wrist-camera poses. These and static-camera poses permit multi-view RGB-D fusion. Thus reconstruction depends on state prediction and calibration as well as depth.

steps.name: Represent heterogeneous robots
steps.detail: States are 16-dimensional absolute dual-arm position/quaternion/gripper vectors; actions are 14-dimensional relative position/axis-angle/gripper vectors. Single-arm data supervise only the first arm. Dataset-specific quantiles normalize values; action scaling omits bias to preserve zero movement.

training.text: Pretraining uses 1,492,026 episodes totaling 5,873.9 hours from AgibotWorld-Beta, DROID, InternA1 variants, RoboCasa MimicGen and RoboTwin 2.0. Videos become 320×256 at 3.75 FPS; Video Depth Anything supplies depth labels. Filtering excludes locomotion, dexterous manipulation, failed episodes and stationary DROID frames.

Pretraining runs 40,000 AdamW steps on 256 H20 GPUs, batch 2,048, peak learning rate 10^-4, 1,000 warmup steps and cosine decay. Loss weights equal one; ANS uses p=0.5. Benchmark fine-tuning uses 32 H20 GPUs, batch 128, 20,000 steps and learning rate 3×10^-5.

Benchmark depth comes from replaying official demonstrations without changing data volume or initial configurations; replay seeds avoid test overlap. RoboCasa uses raw dataset actions. RoboTwin relative actions become absolute end-effector poses using the action chunk’s initial state.

inference.text: Separate UniPC schedules use 10 action steps and 50 video steps for benchmark evaluation, with guidance scale 1.0. Actions can be dispatched immediately when clean; remaining video steps condition on fixed clean states/actions. Depth can be disabled during action decoding.

Physical deployment uses eight steps on an RTX 5090 D, approximately 300 ms per action chunk, and Real-Time Chunking (RTC) to overlap computation with execution. Control runs at 15 Hz, executing 15 actions per chunk with a six-action inference delay.

equations.explanation: Equation (2): wrist-camera pose is the predicted end-effector pose composed with the fixed hand-to-eye calibration transform, providing the moving viewpoint for RGB-D fusion.

Equation (4): t_O and t_a are video and action noise levels; states share t_a. The first branch trains action-conditioned generation; the second biases video toward greater noise while ensuring t_O≥t_a. The mixture probability p is 0.5.

Equations (5–6): modality m is video O, state s or action a. The model predicts velocity from noisy latent z toward the noise-minus-clean target. D-hat and D-star are predicted and target inverse depth; lambda coefficients weight losses.

results.setting: 24 simulated tasks; pretrained then benchmark-fine-tuned model; 100 evaluation episodes per task.
results.interpretation: Strong benchmark performance under differing baseline pretraining. Per-task outcomes include TurnOffStove 35.0% and CloseDrawer 100.0%.

results.setting: 50 AgileX tasks; Clean/Randomized protocols; 100 evaluation episodes per task. Training includes 50 clean and 500 randomized trajectories per task.
results.interpretation: The randomized score concerns specified benchmark variations, not unrestricted real-world generalization.

results.setting: Predictions versus simulator renders during policy execution; pixel metrics use only two static cameras; fused point clouds assess multi-view geometry.
results.metric: PSNR↑, SSIM↑, LPIPS↓, AbsRel↓, delta_1↑, Chamfer Distance↓
results.comparison: Without depth plus DA3: AbsRel 0.1045, CD 0.0401. Robot4DGen: LPIPS 0.1026, CD 0.0134.
results.interpretation: Supports integrated geometry; wrist-camera pixel accuracy is excluded, and CD units are unspecified.

results.setting: Direct Wan2.2 fine-tuning without robotic pretraining; one RTX 3090; five asynchronous action steps versus 25 synchronous steps.
results.metric: Success rate, action latency and reconstruction quality
results.value: Interleaved depth/ANS: 67.8% SR, 1,033 ms; no depth: 63.0%, 1,033 ms.
results.comparison: Sequence depth: 68.7%, 1,888 ms. Synchronous: 66.4%, 4,665 ms. Decoupled asynchronous: 67.2%, 1,033 ms, PSNR 22.60 versus ANS 23.46.
results.interpretation: Depth helps at unchanged decoding latency; sequence depth has better quality but costs more. ANS improves fast-decoding generation quality. This differs from the 79.2% pretrained setting.

results.setting: AC One dual-arm robot; approximately 20 demonstration hours; six trials per setting.
results.metric: Average stage progress (%); time over fully completed episodes only (s)
results.interpretation: Counts represent stages, not successful episodes. Small samples and success-conditioned timing limit reliability and speed conclusions.

limitations.text: The authors identify fixed context without history or autoregressive rollout, and inference delay that leaves the robot acting on older observations. RTC hides pauses but does not eliminate stale predictions.

Comparisons mix published baselines and authors’ implementations with different pretraining; averages lack uncertainty intervals. Physical results chiefly compare XR-0. The authors omitted pi_0.5 from Table 8 after no completed episode and only 25–50% single-earphone progress.

ANS covers inference’s noise ordering and clean-action phase; its two-dimensional training mixture does not establish exact equality with a discrete inference trajectory. Ablations support a quality/latency tradeoff, not universal necessity of explicit depth.

reproduction.text: Reproduction requires the Wan checkpoint, listed data, depth labels, simulator replay, normalization and camera calibration. Physical fine-tuning uses 64 H20 GPUs, batch four per GPU, for 40,000 steps. Software versions, calibration values, full filtering thresholds and a complete frozen-module policy are unspecified.

A smaller proposed check can repeat the no-pretraining RoboCasa ablation with matched data/seeds: compare ANS with independent sampling at the same asynchronous schedule, and depth supervision on/off with depth decoding disabled. Measure policy success separately from reconstruction and latency.

reasoning.text: The catalog is unassigned, so no recorded quadrant can be confirmed or contradicted. The shared bidirectional video/state/action DiT supports a One Model, joint future/action prediction assessment. Depth is auxiliary; action extraction uses no separate inverse-dynamics model and need not wait for completed video.

discussionQuestions: Does depth supervision help after matching large-scale pretraining and multiple seeds?
How does success change with progressively older observations?
How much fused-geometry error comes from wrist-pose prediction rather than depth?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, byline, affiliations and arXiv margin
evidence.detail: Exact title and ten authors match the catalog. The artifact is arXiv:2604.26694v2, dated 7 May 2026; affiliations are Tsinghua University, Xiaomi Robotics, Peking University and CASIA.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 2–3, Section 1; Figure 1
evidence.detail: Motivation combines spatial grounding, unified policy/world prediction and lower action latency; depth adaptation and ANS are the proposed mechanisms.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Eq. (1)
evidence.detail: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, causal VAE, state/action MLPs, clean initial conditions, full attention, view embeddings and temporal RoPE; H=8 and K=32.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1, Eq. (2)
evidence.detail: Fixed static-camera poses and predicted end-effector poses with hand-eye calibration provide extrinsics for multi-view fusion.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 5–6, Section 3.2, Eq. (3); p. 16, Algorithm 1, lines 7–13
evidence.detail: Depth shares the VAE representation, reads main-branch inputs unilaterally and regresses inverse depth. Its branch can be toggled at inference; the text does not state that the shared backbone is frozen.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 3.3, Eq. (4); p. 17, Algorithm 2
evidence.detail: ANS combines clean-action and Beta-coupled branches satisfying t_O≥t_a. States/actions finish first, after which only video updates; actions are available after T_a.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 6–7, Section 3.4, Eqs. (5–6)
evidence.detail: Flow matching predicts noise minus clean latent for video/state/action; inverse-depth MSE supplies geometry supervision. States and actions share a noise level.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Appendix B.1 and Table 5
evidence.detail: Seven dataset rows total 1,492,026 episodes and 5,873.9 hours. Processing uses 320×256 at 3.75 FPS, Video Depth Anything labels and the stated episode/frame exclusions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 17, Appendix B.2, representation and pretraining paragraphs
evidence.detail: States/actions have 16/14 dimensions, single-arm masking and quantile normalization. Pretraining: 256 H20 GPUs, batch 2,048, 40,000 steps, AdamW, peak learning rate 10^-4, 1,000-step warmup, cosine decay, M=10, p=0.5, unit loss weights.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 17–18, Appendix B.2, benchmark fine-tuning and inference
evidence.detail: Fine-tuning: 32 H20 GPUs, batch 128, 20,000 steps, learning rate 3×10^-5. Replay seeds avoid test overlap. Benchmark UniPC uses 10/50 action/video steps, guidance 1.0 and 100 episodes per task.

evidence.location: PDF p. 18, Appendix B.3
evidence.detail: Most baseline values are imported. DreamZero on RoboCasa and UWM on RoboTwin use authors’ Wan2.2-5B implementations. DreamZero lacks robotic pretraining; other baselines have differing robotic pretraining.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 8, Table 1, X-WAM and Cosmos Policy rows
evidence.detail: RoboCasa averages 24 tasks: X-WAM 79.2%, Cosmos Policy 67.1%; no uncertainty intervals appear.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 8, Table 2, X-WAM and Motus rows
evidence.detail: RoboTwin covers 50 tasks and clean/randomized training trajectories. X-WAM scores 89.8/90.7%; Motus 88.7/87.0%.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Table 3, all rows/metric columns; Section 4.2
evidence.detail: X-WAM records 23.46, 0.8942, 0.0513, 0.0349, 0.9738 and 0.0049 for PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, AbsRel, delta_1 and CD. Pixel metrics exclude the wrist camera; point clouds combine viewpoints. CD units and reconstruction sample counts are not given.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Table 4(a–b), all rows; Section 4.3
evidence.detail: Ablations omit robotic pretraining. RTX 3090 latency: no/interleaved depth 1,033 ms at 63.0/67.8% SR; sequence depth 1,888 ms at 68.7%. Synchronous latency is 4,665 ms; decoupled/ANS asynchronous PSNR is 22.60/23.46 with five action steps.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 18–19, Appendix D, Setup; Figure 3
evidence.detail: AC One: one main/two wrist cameras at 320×256; about 20 demonstration hours; 64 H20 GPUs, batch four per GPU, 40,000 fine-tuning steps. Eight-step RTX 5090 D inference takes about 300 ms/chunk; RTC uses 15-Hz control, 15 executed actions and a six-action delay.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 19–20, Appendix D, task design, settings and quantitative-results paragraphs
evidence.detail: Four stages contribute 25% each; six trials per setting test length, placements, tablecloths and distractors. Time averages only completed episodes. The authors omit pi_0.5 after no complete episodes and 25–50% single-earphone progress.

evidence.location: PDF p. 21, Table 8, caption and all rows
PDF p. 21, Figure 4 and caption
evidence.detail: Ten numbered keyframes depict an author-selected representative physical AC One execution; they supply neither continuous timing nor aggregate success.

evidence.location: PDF p. 21, Appendix E
evidence.detail: Fixed-context/no-history and latency limitations remain; RTC does not remove delayed-observation effects. History, KV caching, autoregression and acceleration are future directions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 19, Table 6, CloseDrawer and TurnOffStove rows; p. 20, Table 7, task rows and Average
evidence.detail: RoboCasa success includes CloseDrawer 100.0% and TurnOffStove 35.0%; Table 7 supplies separate clean/randomized per-task RoboTwin outcomes.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 2(a–b) and caption; p. 6, Eqs. (3–4); pp. 16–17, Algorithms 1–2
evidence.detail: The allowed arrow goes from main to depth; the reverse path is crossed out. Joint-noise plots label t_O≥t_a and t_a=0; inference releases actions at T_a while video continues to T_O. Markers agree with the formulation.
